title: Elon Musk with Nikhil Kamath: make more than you take, pursue useful products not money, avoid politics
summary: A wide-ranging conversation covering X, Starlink physics, AI and robotics-driven abundance, and the simulation hypothesis. The business advice for young Indian entrepreneurs: build useful products, aim to make more than you take, and expect to grind hard. He also says to judge companies by their products and team, and that talent is scarce.

principles.text: Don't chase money directly; build useful products and services and money follows as a consequence.
principles.quote: If you do that, then money will come as a natural consequence of that as opposed to pursuing money directly.

principles.text: Be a net value creator: make the output worth more than the input, and make more than you take.
principles.quote: just be focused on having the output be worth more than the input. That are you a value creator? That's what really matters.

principles.text: Making a startup succeed or doing very difficult things requires putting in serious hours.
principles.quote: if you're trying to make a startup succeed or you're trying to make a company do very difficult things then you you you definitely need to put in serious hours.

principles.text: Judge a company by its products and its team, not by daily price swings.
principles.quote: a company is just a group of people assembled to create products and services. So you have to say what are how good are those products and services?

principles.text: Talented people are always scarce, so hunt for the best in the world and pay well above average.
principles.quote: we have a lot of difficulty finding enough talented people to get these difficult tasks done

principles.text: Politics is brutal for businesspeople; stay out of it where possible.
principles.quote: politics is a blood sport, you know? It's like you enter politics, they're going to go for the jugular.
